Methods
The study consisted of two phases of weekly social media posts. In

engagement was monitored. Three different types of posts were

informative content related to research activities; type 2 was image

text caption of the image; and type 3 was image content with people –
scientists working on research activities with a short text caption of
the image.

most audience engagement on LinkedIn, suggesting that using
images of people in combination with short text captions is the most
effective way to engage social media audiences. These findings can

The research idea is innovative, and I appreciate how the authors are trying to do the
operationalization with some acknowledged limits. My suggestion is to have different sections
between Introduction and Theoretical Background (Literature Review). The current introduction
section reads more like a theoretical background. I would suggest having an introduction that
gives a non-technical audience a general overview of the topic. This is important as the authors
are trying to do interdisciplinary research (e.g., communication, social media, sustainability, and
construction).
I am also curious about how the authors address research questions. In my opinion, the research
questions resemble specific and testable hypotheses. If my guess is right, with the same spirit of
reaching a non-technical audience, I would suggest breaking down the theoretical background
per hypothesis.
Kudos for your hard work.

Dear reviewer. Thank you for the suggestions, feedback [行政致谢已隐藏]. We appreciate your recognition of the innovative nature of the presented study and
your acknowledgment of the challenges associated with it. In our study we were guided by
research questions as our research is exploratory and the studied topic is complex. This led us
also in the analysis, results and discussion part. However, we will assure to take into
consideration all the suggestions in the future similar studies that we aim to perform.

The authors are appreciating the critical view of the manuscript and acknowledge the identified
importance of the topics addressed by the reviewer. The modifications of the manuscript
following the recommendations of the reviewer have improved the manuscript and addressed the
feedback given by the reviewer. All the changes are marked with track changes in the Manuscript
file.
Point 1: There is very little engagement with the literature. This is at the beginning of the
paper and is mainly concerned about communciation. However, the realities of scientific
communication through social media have not been explored.
Answer 1: We acknowledge the importance of engaging with the existing literature
comprehensively, therefore we addressed this comment by rewriting the Discussion in order to be

more engaged with the literature presented in the Introduction. In the Introduction section we
provide findings of existing literature on the studied field. The identified gaps led us to create the
main objective of our study. We connected the findings form the existing literature with the main
findings of this study in the Discussion section.
Point 2: The structural characteristics of the 'networks' of the InnoRenew CoE on these three
different channels, have been provided at the beginning of the Materials and methods
section. This demographic data has not been used to evaluate the 'measures of
engagement' on this different platforms.
Answer 2: This was not the goal of our study, however we provided a description of the audience
at the InnoRenew CoE social media channels, since we are aware that the characteristics of the
audience is important for the engagement. We rewrote the Discussion section in order to enhance
this aspect as a limitation of our study, and added the recommendation for future studies.
Point 3: The discussion is mainly based on the number of impressions, shares and
comments. The differences between these 'measures of engagement' by different users has
not been established in enough depth. For example, there is a claim that "users may not be
comfortable commenting on topics connected to sustainable construction, or that they are
not interested in engaging in conversations on social media to develop new relationships."
As far as the paper is concerned, this correlation is now based on any evidence.
Answer 3: We acknowledge that knowing the exact characteristics of the audience, the possible
audience relapse and similar issues is a limitation of our study. We rewrote this part in the
Discussion section to highlight it better. As for the quoted finding of our study regarding users
not being comfortable to comment on topics on social media, this is the interoperation of the
result which is also in line with previous studies that are cited in the manuscript, e.g. (Ellison et
al., 2014)

The research is relevant for communicating about sustainable construction in a research project
dissemination context. As most research dissemination projects have either no communication
budgets or very limited budgets, this study is also relevant from this perspective. The researchers
presented their case study by communicating three types of content distributed across three
different social media platforms. However, most communication campaigns on social media
platforms have budgets for running A/B testing of different messages and testing the
effectiveness on each channel. Therefore, the results of this study are limited to research project
dissemination in a zero-budget context. It is assumed that there was a zero budget for
communication on social media, as this information is not provided. The authors should include as
a limitation the fact that testing the video content was not considered in their experiment.

ssemination
of research findings is common practice among scientists.
Often, this is also a requirement from research funding bodies.
We can define it as a planned process that carefully considers
the intended audience and the contexts in which research
findings will be presented, with the goal of effectively communicate and engage with the target audience through various
interactions (Wilson et al., 2010).
There are several ways to disseminate and communicate about
research. Science communication is about sharing findings,
increasing public appreciation, increasing knowledge, and understanding, influencing opinions, policy preferences and behaviours, and is about promoting diverse science perspectives
for comprehensive societal challenges (Medicine et al., 2017).
As the scientific topics related to environmental issues are complex and hard to understand for the general public (Moser, 2010),
the models of communication must be adopted and include
not only the transfer of information from the messenger to
the audience through a channel, but they must recognize also
the context and the meaning of the message (Jasanoff et al.,
2001). Improving the population’s beliefs about science and
generating social acceptance are also among the aims of science
communication. Just like in the communication literature, also
in science communication we find one-way communication
when scientist share their knowledge to the public, and a
dialogue model, when the public, experts and other stakeholders are engaged in a scientific discussion (Kappel & Holmen,
2019). Social networks are one of the channels offering
the possibility of dialog and they became a crucial part of
communication strategies.
